summary:
Schleswig-Holstein stands under the German national framework. The state has enacted no statute or ordinance specific to trans people, and it has no provision of its own governing where a trans prisoner is held. Placement in a Schleswig-Holstein facility therefore follows the national rules, with no state-level variation layered on top of them.

No trans-specific exception clause of the kind that has drawn constitutional doubt in other states' prison acts exists in Schleswig-Holstein law.

The state's own trans-relevant legislative record is a co-sponsored initiative. Schleswig-Holstein, with Hesse, Berlin, Bremen and Saarland, tabled a joint motion in the Bundesrat for a ban on conversion therapy, presented in plenary on 12 April 2019.
tangentialFactors: No Schleswig-Holstein-specific material adjacent to the visitor assessment appears in the inventory. Prison-placement litigation, airport screening complaints and access disputes in the sauna sector are national in scope and are carried by the national record rather than here.
localsOnly:
Trans residents of Schleswig-Holstein have no state statute or ordinance addressed to them. Legal gender recognition, protection from discrimination and custody placement all run through the national framework, and the state has not enacted a placement rule for trans prisoners.

The state's trans-related legislative action is the 2019 Bundesrat motion on conversion therapy, co-tabled with Hesse, Berlin, Bremen and Saarland and presented in plenary on 12 April 2019.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory holds no Schleswig-Holstein-specific enforcement data, incident reporting or prison-service guidance for trans people, and no finding on gender identity from a state anti-discrimination body. Whether the state will legislate on trans-prisoner placement is not sourced.

Constitutional doubts raised about trans-targeted exception clauses in state prison law are analysed at national level and are carried by the national record; no such clause exists in Schleswig-Holstein law to test them against.
